fields.title: Audit copy-prone workarounds and stale consumer patterns

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: runlimit/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs:410-411 and attempts.rs:262-265 discard catch_unwind results. Dropping the caught Box<dyn Any + Send> runs application payload destructors outside containment. A callback using panic_any(Payload) where Payload::drop panics makes both helpers unwind. Both helpers are used by memory and PostgreSQL backends after state changes; the observer contract says telemetry cannot change admission results. This is a copy-prone catch-and-ignore pattern, not a default panic-hook concern. Two independent external characterization tests ran on Rust 1.100.0/macOS arm64 and confirmed an outer catch_unwind receives Err from each helper. Keep the fix native to Runlimit; do not add a dependency on Batter. Assess payload disposal rather than adding one more catch that can itself discard an arbitrary payload.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Both observer helpers contain payload destruction; string and custom payload cases are tested, including post-mutation backend behavior; document disposal and runtime limits; preserve dependency direction and run required verification.
fields.title: Contain Runlimit observer panic-payload destruction

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: worker_binary.rs:73, producer_worker/worker.rs:58, runtime crate docs and Runledger README use RuntimeShutdownSignal::ctrl_c(). shutdown_signal.rs:143-146 only wraps tokio::signal::ctrl_c, whose pinned Unix source registers SignalKind::interrupt. No SIGTERM listener exists in the native examples. A deployed copy receiving SIGTERM therefore bypasses the illustrated report classification and awaited pool closure. This is source-confirmed; no new SIGTERM subprocess experiment was run. Prefer a native library-owned SIGINT/SIGTERM signal constructor and adopt it in worker entrypoints; preserve application-installed signal policy and native ownership.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Native worker examples and quick-start handle SIGINT and SIGTERM through accounted shutdown; subprocess tests prove classification and cleanup; setup errors retained; Unix-only; public API review and docs synchronized.
fields.title: Give native worker examples a Unix termination signal path

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: runledger/runledger-runtime/examples/producer_worker/worker.rs:51 prints worker ready before Supervisor::builder_from_env(...).build() at lines 53-55. README embeds it at line 296 and instructs users to wait for that text at line 359. The example may report ready before supervisor construction fails or any loop initializes. Native startup_observer already exists. Keep definition availability distinct from worker initialization; do not imply that the observer proves database health or durable processing. Source-confirmed, not newly executed against a startup-failure fixture.

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: JobProgressUpdate (types/lifecycle.rs:70-80), update_job_progress and update_job_progress_for_lease (queue/lifecycle/progress.rs:312-351) are deprecated since 0.11.0 but still exported through jobs and the prelude in 0.13.0. Unlike harmless aliases, the old input preserves arbitrary JobStage writes and funnels them into shared SQL. queue_running_progress.rs:323 explicitly tests setting a claimed job back to Scheduled; typed ordinary progress cannot express that. This compatibility branch preserves a known weaker lifecycle shape, and the prelude makes it easy for a new agent to adopt. Decide a staged public cut/compatibility quarantine after checking real downstream needs; do not alter historical database migrations. Inventory older 0.1.2/0.8/0.11 aliases separately and distinguish inert aliases from invariant-restoring shims.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Recorded compatibility decision and bounded retirement scope; new-consumer guidance/prelude no longer present stage-bearing progress as ordinary integration; hard-cut obligations met if removal approved; preserve supported running/ordinary progress behavior and failure tests.

data.text: Codex review (gpt-6.2-astra, xhigh) of the uncommitted upgrade found, and source inspection confirmed: (1) SQLx 0.9.1 new_without_pgpass reads ambient PGHOSTADDR into hostaddr, which connect prefers over the URL host; batter-sqlx ConnectionPlan::resolve and runledger-test-support fixture URLs were redirectable. (2) #4375 re-send also covers simple-query raw_sql and reads only the SQLSTATE, so a statement with earlier non-transactional effects that raises 26000/0A000 repeats them outside a transaction (review reproduced on PG18). My earlier 'not a replay' note was wrong. (3) With statement cache disabled, persistent queries use the unnamed statement and the custom-type re-parse only runs for nonpersistent ones: first uncached enum query in a transaction fails 26000 (review reproduced on PG18). User chose upgrade + mitigate. Mitigation: new public batter_sqlx::test_support::AmbientHostAddress, resolution refuses when PGHOSTADDR is present (injectable lookup, offline unit test); Runledger shared fixture startup asserts PGHOSTADDR absent before any container (unit tests). (2) and (3) are disclosed in guarantees and the ecosystem upgrade record; Batter cannot disable them.

fields.description: Observed 2026-11-18 on macOS (aarch64), pinned Rust 1.100.0, during bash scripts/verify.sh workspace-tests: watchdog::tests::parent_unwind_kills_reaps_and_joins_capture_reader (crates/batter-core/tests/non_yielding/watchdog_tests.rs:102) failed with 'unwind cleanup took 5.005681584s; expected completion before 5s'. The bound deliberately includes child startup. The same target then passed 3/3 alone (cargo test -p batter-core --test non_yielding --locked). Found while verifying batter-c5ci, which does not touch batter-core. Do not relax the semantic bound without showing that the 5 s limit still distinguishes the 10 s child emergency exit; consider separating startup from the measured unwind interval.
fields.title: batter-core non_yielding parent_unwind_kills_reaps_and_joins_capture_reader flakes in the workspace matrix

data.text: Cause: watchdog_tests.rs measured the 5 s bounds from spawn (FixtureChild::started), so loaded-matrix child startup consumed the unwind/exit budget. First verify.sh rerun after the initial fix exposed the same class in parent_pipe_closure_ends_blocked_runtime_without_cleanup (watchdog kill at 5.001 s after runtime-drop-started; expected PARENT_GONE). Fix: parent_unwind times unwind from after fixture-entered (< EXIT_LIMIT) and separately asserts spawn-to-cleanup < EMERGENCY_LIMIT (child arms its emergency exit after spawn, so this exactly excludes waiting for exit 75). parent_pipe_closure waits EXIT_LIMIT from closure; exact code 74 still separates it from emergency 75. Mutation evidence (macOS aarch64, Rust 1.100.0): FixtureChild::drop changed to child.wait() -> parent_unwind fails 'unwind cleanup took 9.995s'; launch EOF exit replaced with park -> parent_pipe_closure fails with watchdog SIGKILL. Target passes 50/50 with both fixes.

fields.description: ADR-010 recurring-defect assessment from batter-c5ci. SQLx 0.9.1 (#4514, libpq semantics) applies ambient PGHOSTADDR to every PgConnectOptions URL parse that omits hostaddr, and offers no env-free constructor or hostaddr reset. Point guards in ConnectionPlan::resolve and Runledger shared startup were followed by a second review finding the same redirect at other sites: batter-sqlx and Runlimit live-test helpers (e.g. profile_privileges_live, runlimit test_pool), Runledger drop_database after startup and the delayed-startup test, FixtureScope/FixtureSuite template initializers, scripts/test_runledger_tools.py live CLI test, and the owned_pool/verification facade examples. About 71 URL-based connection sites in ~40 files. Cause: upstream protocol change plus a Batter design gap (no library-owned URL-to-options boundary). Candidate remedy: one public batter-sqlx constructor that refuses PGHOSTADDR (and documents the process-environment precondition), adopted by every internal site and example, plus a source-inventory test like crates/batter/tests/panic_hook_ownership.rs forbidding raw URL parsing/connect(url) outside it; Python children scrub PGHOSTADDR. Alternative: keep SQLx 0.9.0 and request an env-free constructor upstream. Public-contract change: needs user decision.
fields.title: Central PostgreSQL URL boundary that refuses ambient PGHOSTADDR under SQLx 0.9.1

ADR-010 recurrence assessment after Codex round 4 (gpt-6.2-astra xhigh, branch 71c8410f): 6 confirmed findings. (1) template initializers check only env PGHOSTADDR, not socket-shadowed URL hostaddr; (2) exempt native roots (runledger-tui, two native examples) diverge from libpq: PGHOST=/tmp + URL hostaddr connects to socket; (3) runledger-test-support with_database_name drops the admin URL query, so host/hostaddr endpoint params differ between admin and lease connections under 0.9.1; (4) refresh_runledger_sqlx: psql honours URL hostaddr but SQLx CLI uses the socket; (5) scan misses PgListener::connect(url) and runledger_postgres::DbPool alias; (6) literal connect_lazy exemption admits live URLs (40 literal sites). Classification: upstream protocol change (SQLx 0.9.1 hostaddr semantics: env, socket precedence, query handling) plus an enforcement design gap (text scan cannot resolve aliases/types). Point fixes cover more cases of the same protocol. Candidate remedy: boundary refuses hostaddr in env and URL everywhere (removes socket-shadow and derived-URL classes), and replace call-form text rules with clippy disallowed-methods (alias/type resolved), keeping text rules only for parse(); rewrite inert lazy placeholders. Alternatives: point-patch the six; or revert to SQLx 0.9.0. Paused for user decision.

User chose: refuse hostaddr everywhere + Clippy enforcement. New class: cross-parser divergence between SQLx, tokio-postgres (harness) and libpq (psql): query host= is an override in SQLx but a fallback in tokio-postgres; retained port= gives tokio-postgres two ports; keyword/value connection strings pass URL-only checks into psql; Cargo [env] DATABASE_URL force can differ from the preflighted URL. Paused for user decision.

User chose strict canonical URL subset. Round 8 fixes (next commit): canonical rules in batter_sqlx::connect_options (NoncanonicalUrl + exhaustive NoncanonicalReason), runledger-test-support, Runlimit helper and Python refresh (keyword/value refused); Cargo probe also checks compiler DATABASE_URL equality (forced [env] test passes); rustdoc recipe fixed and doc-comment Rust fences scanned; reference state live test validates before harness start; probe test copies rust-toolchain.toml. Local: fmt, budget, clippy, rustdoc, unit/doc/scan tests, Docker runledger-test-support + proxies, reference configuration suite, Python 3.9 and 3.15, repo scripts.

Round 9 (gpt-6.2-astra xhigh): 7 findings inside the round-8 subset (it was a blocklist). Tightened to an explicit allowlist in all four validators: explicit host+port+database (socket encoded in authority), parameters limited to sslmode/sslrootcert/sslcert/sslkey/application_name/options/user/password/dbname once each, raw query '+' and raw '@' outside userinfo refused, decoded/encoded multi-host refused; PGSERVICE refused in refresh; reference handoff writes explicit port; repo URLs/README examples gained ports. Behavior change for consumers of the unreleased boundary: ports and databases now mandatory. Local: full workspace lib+tests (incl Docker), doc tests, reference configuration, clippy, rustdoc, budget, Python 3.9/3.15, repo scripts. Trend 6,4,9,4,7,7.

Round 10 (gpt-6.2-astra xhigh, 4fb6de24): 11 findings; trend 6,4,9,4,7,7,11 - diverging. P1: template initializer can target admin db via ?dbname= retained by harness; paths //jobs and /one/../jobs normalize differently (SQLx vs tokio-postgres vs libpq). P2: percent-encoded TCP host read differently; tokio-postgres rejects sslcert/sslkey/sslrootcert and non-lowercase/verify sslmode; empty dbname falls back to login db; raw query syntax (?key, a=b=c) lost by form decoding; reference state probe should use preflight handoff; PGSERVICE affects libpq claim; pool_in accepts unrestricted native options (opaque endpoint type suggested). P3: typed FromStr::from_str form; runlimit lib.rs live-test command uses hostless URL. Assessment: since round 8 the public boundary promises three-parser agreement over arbitrary text, which is open-ended; most new divergences predate SQLx 0.9.1. Candidate remedy: narrow the public guarantee to SQLx endpoint selection (no ambient/declared hostaddr, explicit host/port/db) and, where one URL feeds several clients (fixture harness, refresh script), re-serialize a minimal canonical URL from parsed components instead of validating text. Paused for user decision.

fields.description: SQLx 0.9.1 (sqlx-postgres options/mod.rs make_socket_path) checks a Unix socket (host=/dir, or PGHOST/socket discovery for a hostless URL) before a declared hostaddr, so postgres:///db?hostaddr=127.0.0.1 connects through a socket. PostgreSQL 18 libpq docs: TCP 'is always used when a nonempty string is specified' for hostaddr. Draft an upstream issue (transact-rs/sqlx) with a minimal reproduction; posting it publicly needs explicit user approval. Batter fixture paths already refuse hostaddr (UnsupportedHarnessEndpoint::HostAddress).
fields.title: Report SQLx 0.9.1 socket-over-hostaddr divergence from libpq upstream

fields.description: Codex round 10 (ADR-010): protected batter_sqlx::pool_in accepts unrestricted native PgConnectOptions, so a caller can apply .hostaddr(...) or a host setter to socket options after any validation. Assess an opaque endpoint value consumed by pool_in with native options kept on low_level. pool_in is released in 0.0.1, so this is a public hard cut needing Breaking changelog, Migration rustdoc and a deprecation decision; out of scope for batter-c5ci.
fields.title: Opaque validated endpoint for protected pool_in

fields.description: Observed 2026-11-18 on macOS aarch64, Rust 1.100.0, during cargo test --workspace --all-features --lib --tests with load average ~16: job_enqueue_intents::promotion_row_lock_wait_is_bounded_while_holding_retention_fence failed once; it then passed 3/3 alone (6.5 s each). Found while verifying batter-c5ci, which does not change runledger-postgres code. Do not relax the bound without showing it still detects an unbounded wait.
fields.title: runledger-postgres promotion_row_lock_wait_is_bounded_while_holding_retention_fence flakes under load

data.text: User agreed to the narrowed design. b74231ea reverts the unreleased app-wide boundary (connect_options, canonical URL rules, Clippy denylist, source scan, ~110 rewritten sites). New: test_support/endpoint.rs parses the harness admin URL once with tokio-postgres 0.7.18 and maps the typed Config into SQLx options with the recorded database (UnsupportedHarnessEndpoint/HarnessEndpointReason; public harness_connect_options, harness_admin_connect_options); template initializers get a rebuilt URL round-tripped through both parsers; reference fixture tests use the helpers or preflight options; refresh script parses once, psql via PG* vars in a scrubbed env, SQLx via rebuilt URL, Cargo probe; Runledger container-only PGHOSTADDR refusal. Local: fmt, budget, workspace clippy, rustdoc -D warnings, workspace lib+tests (one load flake filed batter-cub5, passes 3/3 alone), doc tests, Python 3.9/3.15, repo scripts. Follow-ups: batter-c5ci.2 (upstream socket/hostaddr), batter-c5ci.3 (pool_in endpoint). Review stop rule agreed: no P0/P1 against stated invariants; P2/P3 filed as Beads.

fields.description: Codex round 11 (P2): scripts/refresh_runledger_sqlx.py cargo_compiler_endpoint compiles option_env!("DATABASE_URL") into the probe; with CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR outside the temp dir the password can persist in the executable, dep-info and incremental cache. Compare effective values in a Cargo-launched process (e.g. a build script or runner env dump of a digest) without embedding the URL.
fields.title: Keep DATABASE_URL credentials out of the refresh Cargo probe's build artifacts

fields.description: Codex round 11 (P2): a Cargo [env] PGOPTIONS such as -c search_path=shadow,public reaches the query macros but not psql or SQLx CLI checks, so unqualified checked queries could describe a shadow table. Extend the refresh Cargo probe to refuse PGOPTIONS (and other session-affecting PG* settings) for the compiler, or pass them explicitly to every client.
fields.title: Refuse compiler-side PG* settings that change schema selection during metadata refresh

fields.description: Codex round 11 (P2): crates/batter-sqlx test_support endpoint and plan success tests parse SQLx options in the runner's real environment; PGAPPNAME or PGHOSTADDR in the shell makes them fail (RoundTrip or the production refusal) instead of exercising the intended path. Run success cases in a cleared child environment and keep hostile-environment cases separate; do not weaken the runtime guard.
fields.title: Isolate offline fixture endpoint tests from the caller's PG* environment

data.text: Round 11 (policy-scoped prompt; codex review cannot combine --base with a prompt, so scope given in prompt): 5 P1 + 7 P2. Fixed all P1 (dot-only db names, live test setup env, delayed-startup guard via start_postgres, non-UTF-8 socket path, load_balance_hosts) and 4 cheap P2 (port 0, strict UTF-8, socket colon, empty password). Filed P2: batter-c5ci.4/.5/.6. Local gates all pass.

fields.description: Codex round 12 (P2): HarnessEndpoint::options starts from PgConnectOptions::new_without_pgpass, which imports PGOPTIONS, PGAPPNAME and PGPASSWORD; when the admin URL omits those fields the conditional setters leave the ambient values in direct fixture and diagnostic pools, while the template path refuses the same configuration at its round-trip check. Map absent values explicitly (or refuse them) the same way on both paths.
fields.title: Stop ambient PGOPTIONS, PGAPPNAME and PGPASSWORD leaking into direct fixture pools

fields.description: Codex round 12 (P2): cargo_compiler_endpoint uses cargo run without selecting the host target; with build.target set for another architecture the probe needs a target linker and runner. Use a host-executed observation of Cargo's effective compiler environment (for example a build script, which always runs on the host) instead of running a target binary.
fields.title: Make the refresh Cargo probe work when build.target names another architecture

data.text: Round 12 (5 P1): user approved narrowing - DNS round-robin and child-process environments are documented preconditions, not findings; sqlx.toml database-url-var (confirmed in sqlx-cli 0.9.1 opt.rs:461, sqlx-toml default feature) now refused by the refresh; P2s filed .7/.8. One final capped confirming round follows, then stop and land.

fields.description: Final Codex round (P2): for postgres://user@localhost:/db urlsplit().port is None, so refresh_runledger_sqlx.parse_database_url keeps the colon in the host: psql gets PGHOST=localhost: and SQLx gets [localhost:]:5432; an encoded socket directory silently gains a trailing ':'. Separate the delimiter even when the port field is empty (or refuse an empty port).
fields.title: Strip an empty port delimiter from the refresh DATABASE_URL host

fields.description: Final Codex round (P2): cargo_compiler_endpoint uses subprocess.run(timeout=300), which kills only Cargo; a stalled compiler or wrapper child can outlive the probe after its temp build directory is removed. Use the bounded process-group cleanup from runledger_source.run/parallel_process while keeping the probe's output private.
fields.title: Bound the refresh Cargo probe with process-group cleanup on timeout

data.text: Final capped round (round 13): 5 P1 + 2 P2 + 2 P3 against the stated invariant and preconditions. Fixed all P1 (fixture bracketed host names; Runledger owned URL pins hostaddr=127.0.0.1 and derived URLs keep query minus dbname; refresh sqlx.toml case-insensitive, TCP host chars SQLx resolves as written, probe expected URL via stdin) and both P3 doc corrections; P2 filed batter-c5ci.9/.10. Assumption verification (2026-11-19). Probes vs SQLx 0.9.1/tokio-postgres 0.7.18: URL hostaddr overrides ambient PGHOSTADDR (SQLx and psql 18 confirmed; unpinned URL follows the ambient address); SQLx keeps TCP authority hosts percent-encoded while tokio-postgres decodes; SQLx trims edge brackets on connect and to_url_lossy panics on '[host'; tokio-postgres decodes %5B. Live suites on Docker postgres:18 (SCRAM): SQLx live 194/194 across 8 targets; reference live 73 + session + provider-state probes pass.
